subject: Crestview certification sprint plan & load targets

Cc: monica.patel@redwood.com
Date: 2027-04-04T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Crestview certification sprint plan & load targets

Hi Emma,

Thanks again for the demo last week — really appreciated the detail from your platform team. Per our conversation, attached is a proposed certification sprint we use to validate throughput + latency gates before handoff to production. High level:

- Smoke (Janitor): single-node sanity checks, model/endpoint correctness, basic tokenization verification.
- Scale (Throughput): sustained RPS sweep to verify batch sizing and autoscale behavior.
- Soak (Stability): 1–2 hour soak at target load to catch memory/latency drift.

Suggested targets for the Crestview conversational workload (based on sample traces you shared):
- Sustained throughput target: 20 RPS (client-level).
- Average request size: ~180 tokens (post-tokenize).
- 95th percentile latency: <= 350 ms (server-side, request->first-byte).
- 99th percentile latency: <= 650 ms under sustained load.
- Burst concurrency: up to 60 concurrent requests.

We propose running the scale + soak window on Apr 6 (US business hours). Deliverables we'll provide after the run: run-results-20270406.csv, telem-dump for 95/99 analysis, and a short findings deck.

Attached: mutual action plan (map-crestview.docx) and load scripts (crestview-load-scripts.yml). Can you confirm: (1) that Apr 6 works for your platform team, (2) the contact who will own test infra on your side, and (3) whether we should run tests in our Hosted endpoint or your Dedicated environment?

If helpful, I can set a 30m alignment call — happy to do that tomorrow.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com

Emma / Crestview platform team — looping in Laura from Infra so we can confirm test topology and VPC connectivity. Quick answers and test steps below: 

- Tokenization: our runner uses the same tokenizer as the model binary. For any pre-tokenized counts you have, we'll validate a small sample to reconcile (see next).
- VPC/Dedicated runs: yes — we support in-place testing pointed at a customer-managed VPC endpoint. We'll need a short-lived tunnel + the IP allowlist (see MAP section 3.2).

Proposed test steps (detailed in attached runbook):
1) Verify sample traces (we'll exchange a tiny sample file of 100 requests).
2) Smoke run (1k requests) to confirm tokenization parity.
3) Throughput sweep: 5, 10, 15, 20 RPS each for 10 minutes.
4) Soak: 2-hour run at 20 RPS; collect full telemetry.

Concrete latency buckets we'll collect: p50/p95/p99, tail latency (p999 sample), cpu/gpu utilization, queue depths, and kernel-level stall metrics. If any gate is missed we capture the failing trace and recommend config changes (batch size, KV cache warmup, quantization profile).

Attachments: crestview-load-scripts.yml (contains Locust + runner config), map-crestview.docx (mutual action plan).

Laura — can you confirm which infra owner from Redwood should be on the Apr 6 run and if Platform needs a pre-check window Apr 5 15:00 PT?

Thanks,
Monica Patel
